claims.text: The initially homogeneous, nominally single-phase high-entropy alloy has high toughness under moderate loading conditions.
Severe mechanical loading induces localized compositional segregation in the alloy.
Severe mechanical loading induces localized ordering in the alloy.
Stress-induced segregation and ordering mediate a rapid loss of toughness.
Stress-induced segregation and ordering mediate a transition to brittle fracture.
The loading-induced segregation and ordering occur particularly along grain boundaries or within deformation bands.
Severe loading activates atomic-scale diffusion and rearrangement.
Loading-activated diffusion and atomic rearrangement produce localized compositional fluctuations and ordered regions.
Localized compositional fluctuations and ordered regions disrupt uniform deformation.
Disruption of uniform deformation reduces ductility and promotes crack initiation.
Reduced ductility and enhanced crack initiation result in brittle fracture.
Under severe loading, high-resolution TEM or neutron diffraction will detect localized ordered or segregated regions.
The detected ordered or segregated regions will correlate with a marked decrease in toughness relative to moderate-loading specimens.
Severe loading will shift fracture behavior from ductile to brittle relative to the baseline.
At low strain rate or room temperature, the alloy retains a homogeneous phase and high toughness without significant microstructural evolution.
The transition occurs only beyond a loading-dependent strain-rate and/or temperature threshold that triggers segregation.
Below the transition threshold, the alloy microstructure remains stable.
